# Evaluation

How well does the pipeline extract, validate, split and cross-check invoices, and what does
it cost? Measured end to end, through the real API and worker, with the real LLM provider,
on a labelled synthetic dataset. Run it yourself with `make eval` (a few cents of API
credits; see [How to run](#how-to-run)).

## Method

**Dataset** (`eval/dataset/`, regenerated byte-identically by `make eval-dataset`, seed
20261114): 55 labelled invoices in 52 files (17 dev, 38 test: 26 clean and 12 "hard").

| What | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Digital PDFs | 15 | three layouts, Helvetica / Times / DejaVu |
| Scanned-style JPEGs | 8 | rasterised at 200 dpi, rotated 2-5°, blurred, Gaussian noise, JPEG quality 45-75 |
| Image-only (scanned) PDFs | 2 | same degradation, no text layer, so OCR is required |
| XLSX invoices | 5 | key/value block above an item table, real date cells |
| CSV invoices | 5 | the same shape as text |
| Batch PDF | 6 invoices, 9 pages | 1-3 pages each; one 3-page invoice has no "Page k of N" |
| Excel ledger | 1 | for the batch, with 4 planted findings |
| Purchase-order PDF | 1 | for one invoice, with a line differing in quantity and unit price |
| Dev: no-subtotal invoices | 2 | digital PDFs without a subtotal line, one with tax and one without (added to cover the line-sum fix on dev) |
| **Hard subset** (test only) | 12 | heavy noise and blur (2), low-resolution phone photos with shear and uneven light (2), 8-12° rotation (2), faint low-contrast scans (2), crowded layouts with 22-26 line items (digital and scanned), two-column layouts with a "Ship To" distractor (digital and scanned) |

Variation built in: BDT, USD and EUR (as codes or as `Tk`/`$`/`€`), European number style
(`1.234,50`), six date formats including 4 genuinely ambiguous ones (`04/05/2026`), 1-6 line
items, and missing due dates, customers, tax lines, subtotals and currencies. Also 4
deliberately wrong totals, 1 due date before the invoice date, and a duplicate pair (a
digital PDF and a scanned copy of it, uploaded after the original).

**Ground truth** (`eval/dataset/labels/*.json`): every field as printed (null when absent),
line items, ambiguous fields, expected validation flags, the batch's page ranges and the
planted cross-check findings. Expected flags come from each document's planted design,
not from running the app's own rules, which would be circular. For example, a correct
invoice with no subtotal line expects no line-sum flag, even if a rule would raise one.

**Split:** about 40% dev, 60% test, stratified by file type. The batch, the ledger, the
duplicate pair and the hard subset are test only. Prompts and rules are tuned only on dev;
the headline is test. "Test, clean" (26 invoices) stays the same set in every run, so runs
compare; the hard subset is always reported in its own row, never mixed in. Each addition
to the generator uses its own random seed, so earlier files stay byte-identical.

**Isolation:** `make eval` runs in its own compose project (`invoice-eval`) with a fresh
database. Duplicate detection and the assistant look at every document in the database,
so your own documents would otherwise change the results.

### What the metrics mean

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| Field accuracy | Share of the 9 header fields (number, dates, supplier, customer, currency, subtotal, tax, total) that are right. "Right" includes correctly empty (truth null, nothing given), and for an ambiguous date, null *with* an `AMBIGUOUS_DATE` flag. Money is compared as Decimal, dates as ISO, currency as an ISO code, names casefolded, and invoice numbers by the app's key (`No. 247` = `247`). |
| False-fill rate | Of the fields that are not printed, the share where the system gave a value anyway. This is the "invented value" rate (CLAUDE.md rule 3). |
| Missing rate | Of the fields that are printed, the share where the system gave nothing (not counting flagged ambiguous dates). |
| Line items P / R / F1 | A predicted line matches a true one when the description is at least 80% similar and the line total is exactly equal. |
| Flag precision / recall | Over validation codes the document determines (missing fields, total and line-sum mismatches, ambiguous dates, date order). `LOW_CONFIDENCE` depends on the model, so it isn't scored; duplicates and cross-checks are scored separately. |
| Documents processed | Files that ended `processed` or `needs_review`, not `failed`. |
| Time | Job start to finish in the worker, per document and per page (queue wait excluded). Spreadsheets count as one page. |
| Cost | Provider-reported tokens × the prices in `.env` (`LLM_PRICE_*_PER_MTOK`). |

## Headline

Test split, synthetic data, OpenAI `gpt-6-luna`. **The headline is the first row:** the
held-out test results measured *before* the line-sum rule was fixed. The other rows are
labelled for what they are.

| Run | Field accuracy | False fills / missing | Line items F1 | Flags precision / recall | Segmentation, cross-checks, duplicates | Assistant (15 Q) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Headline: test, before the line-sum fix** (run 2, `2026-11-13T20-27-48Z`) | **100%** | **0% / 0%** | **100%** | **93.8% / 100%** | 6/6, 6/6, 1/1 | 14/15 |
| After the line-sum fix, same test set (run 3, `2026-11-13T21-05-25Z`) | 100% | 0% / 0% | 100% | 100% / 100% | 6/6, 6/6, 1/1 | 14/15 |
| Latest, after the search and embedder fixes (run 4, `2026-11-13T22-24-22Z`) | 100% | 0% / 0% | 100% | 100% / 100% | 6/6, 6/6, 1/1 | 15/15 |
| **Hard subset, test** (12 invoices, run 4): the realistic counterpart, *before* the photo work | **75.0%** | – / 13.9% (11.1% wrong) | **85.9%** | 7 of 7 invoices with an error were flagged for review | – | – |
| **Hard subset, test, after** photo preprocessing (flatten) and the vision fallback (run 5, `2026-11-14T01-45-58Z`) | **88.9%** | – / 7.4% (3.7% wrong) | **89.4%** | 6 of 7 invoices with an error were flagged for review | – | – |
| Clean test, same run 5 (no regression) | 100% | 0% / 0% | 100% | 100% / 100% | 6/6, 6/6, 1/1 | 15/15 |
| *Hard dev set* (12 dev invoices, the only set the photo work was tuned on): before / after | 79.6% / 94.5% (bench), 94.4% (run 5) | – | – / 96.1% (run 5) | – | – | – |

The line-sum bug was found on the held-out test split, so the post-fix test number partly
measures data that informed the fix and is no longer an untouched held-out result. Reporting
the pre-fix result as the headline, with the post-fix result clearly labelled beside it
(and the fix also confirmed on two new dev invoices), keeps the headline honest while still
showing that the fix works.

The photo work was developed and measured only on a separate hard **dev** set (same kinds of
damage, different seed). The hard test files were not looked at or tuned on, so the hard
test before/after rows are a held-out measurement.

The clean 100% says the pipeline handles clean, machine-generated documents; the hard rows
say what happens when the image is bad. None of the hard subset's fields are left
unprinted, so it has no false-fill rate. Its flags aren't "planted", so precision doesn't
apply. The useful question is whether a wrong reading reaches review unflagged: in run 4
it never did; in run 5, one of seven did (a phone photo whose amounts all add up; see
[What the runs found](#what-the-runs-found)). The dashboard shows the latest run.

## What the runs found

Four full runs, all kept in `eval/results/`. The generated section above is run 4.

**Run 1** (`2026-11-13T20-17-20Z.json`): test field accuracy 97.9%, flag precision 79.0%.

| Failure | Where | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 dates missing on XLSX invoices, plus 5 false `MISSING_REQUIRED` flags. Evidence was `Invoice Date \| 2026-10-03 00:00:00`; predicted: none | dev (inv-10, inv-39) and test | Excel date cells reach the model as text with a time part; `parse_date` accepted only `YYYY-MM-DD` | **Fixed** (`e0433db`). Found on the dev split, so not tuning on test |
| Purchase-order cross-check scored 0/2 | dev | Bug in the **scorer**: line-level messages name the line, not the invoice. The system had reported both planted mismatches | Scorer fixed (`1e01764`) |
| Assistant Q5 marked wrong for "due **March 25, 2026**" against 2026-03-25 | assistant eval | Bug in the **scorer** (plain substring match) | Scorer fixed (`cc3dbfd`) |

**Run 2** (`2026-11-13T20-27-48Z.json`, the headline):

- **False `LINE_ITEMS_SUM_MISMATCH` on a correct invoice (inv-12, test).** With no subtotal
  line, the rule compared the sum of line items with the *total*, which includes tax. Ground
  truth deliberately didn't expect the flag. **Fixed afterwards** (`7a98a43`): without a
  subtotal, lines are compared with total − tax (or the total when there's no tax), within
  `MONEY_TOLERANCE`. Unit tests cover both cases, and two new **dev** invoices (inv-41 with
  tax, inv-42 without; `370c411`) cover it outside the test split. Run 3: test flag
  precision 100%, dev 100%, and the planted wrong total without a subtotal (inv-30) is still
  flagged.
- **Assistant Q10** ("On which page of eval-batch.pdf does the Umbrella Trading invoice
  start?"): it answered "I found no matching Umbrella Trading invoice". **Cause** (asked 8
  times with the real model): it chose keyword search 7 times, often with "Umbrella Trading
  invoice start page in eval-batch.pdf". Keyword search required *every* word, and "start",
  "page" and the file name aren't printed, so it returned nothing. Twice the model then
  concluded the invoice didn't exist. These were ruled out: the semantic threshold (UT-5
  scored 0.38-0.67 against 0.20), the supplier filter and the batch invoice mapping (all
  found page 2). **Fixed** (`a9080d4`): when no page has every word, keyword search returns
  pages with some of them, ranked by `ts_rank` and marked `partial_match`; queries with
  search operators get no fallback. Then 8/8 on the same question, and `make
  assistant-eval` 15/15.

**Run 4** (`2026-11-13T22-24-22Z.json`, with the hard subset):

- **The first attempt hung**: the worker sat 43 minutes with 40 jobs queued. The crowded
  invoices' pages are about 500 word-pieces (mostly numbers), and torch 2.15's fused SDPA
  attention never returns on CPU (aarch64, more than one thread) for inputs over about 128
  tokens. The encode runs in a thread that a job timeout can't cancel, and it holds the
  embedder lock. **Fixed** (`6afadf5`): the embedding model loads with eager attention (same
  vectors: cosine 1.0, max difference 1e-7; 0.25 s for that page). Regression tests fail
  without the fix. A real invoice with a long table would have hit this in production.
- **Hard subset results by kind:** rotated, crowded and two-column documents were read
  correctly; the errors come from image quality.

  | Kind | Field accuracy | Line items F1 | What went wrong |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | phone_photo (2) | 11.1% | 62.5% | OCR misreads: "Alpine Strumen {SAG", "Tost Caments lta", tax 150.24 → 130.24 |
  | noisy_blur (2) | 55.6% | 0% | "HD-2026-3tt", "HO-2026-322", subtotal 307.59 → 307.53; dates read as "2020-00-29" so left empty |
  | faint (2) | 83.3% | 57.1% | subtotal and tax lines not read; some line items lost |
  | rotated (2), crowded (2), two-column (2) | 100% | 96-100% | one line of 24 misread on the crowded scan |

  Every error is a misreading of the printed text, and **no value was invented**. All 7 hard
  invoices with an error were flagged for review (`LINE_ARITHMETIC`,
  `LINE_ITEMS_SUM_MISMATCH` or `MISSING_REQUIRED`), so none would pass unreviewed. The
  arithmetic checks are what catch misread digits.
- **Speed:** clean documents p50 9.3 s and p95 15 s; hard documents p50 14 s and p95 47 s
  (heavy OCR). The run took 7 minutes and cost about $0.05 at the given prices.

**Run 5** (`2026-11-14T01-45-58Z.json`, photo preprocessing and the vision fallback):

- **How the steps were chosen.** On the hard dev set only (`make hard-dev-bench`, results in
  `eval/results/hard-dev-bench-2026-11-14-preprocessing.json`; OCR confidence / field
  accuracy over 12 invoices):

  | Photo steps | OCR confidence | Field accuracy | Kept? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | none (before) | 80.7 | 79.6% | – |
  | flatten (shadow / uneven-light removal by background division) | 86.5 | 94.5% | **yes** |
  | CLAHE (local contrast) | 78.4 | 78.7% | no: worse alone and on top of flatten (92.6%) |
  | warp (page edges + perspective) | 80.7 | 79.6% | not by default: never fired, because the synthetic photos have no page edges in frame. It is tested on a camera-projected image (corners within 2.4 px, aspect 1.416 vs 1.414) and available as `OCR_PHOTO_STEPS=warp,flatten` |

  The photo-vs-scan decision was right on all 12 dev invoices: only the two phone photos
  got the photo steps, and every scan's result was identical with and without them.
- **Hard test subset, by kind** (run 4 → run 5): phone photos 11.1% → **94.4%** field
  accuracy (line F1 62.5% → 87.5%); rotated, crowded and two-column unchanged at 100%;
  faint 83.3% → 83.3%; noisy and blurred 55.6% → 55.6% (line F1 0% → 20%). Clean test
  results stayed at 100%, and the assistant at 15/15.
- **The vision fallback made 0 calls.** It is used only when a page's OCR confidence
  stays below `OCR_MIN_CONFIDENCE` (60). After preprocessing, every hard page scored
  above that: the noisy scans read at about 74-80 confidence, but with wrong characters
  ("HD-2026-3tt", "Sarnple Retad ld"). So the remaining hard-test errors are confidently
  wrong OCR, which a confidence threshold cannot catch. The fallback works end to end in
  tests (an unreadable scan is read from the image, marked `vision` and sent to review),
  but this run doesn't measure its accuracy. Raising the threshold or triggering on failed
  checks would need measuring on the hard dev set first; that hasn't been done.
- **One error reached review unflagged:** hard-03 (phone photo). Its header fields are all
  right, but a line item doesn't match the label, and no amount check fired (its numbers
  still add up). Misread text that keeps the arithmetic consistent is something the
  current checks don't cover.
- **Cost:** about $0.001 per document, $0.065 for the whole run (64 files plus
  cross-checks and the assistant eval).

## Limitations (read before trusting the numbers)

- **Synthetic is not real.** Every document is clean, machine-generated text in a handful of
  fonts. Real invoices have logos, stamps, handwriting, multi-column layouts, merged table
  cells, crumpled phone photos and Bengali text. Treat these numbers as an **upper bound**.
  The real test is `eval/dataset/real/` (template provided; label your own invoices and
  run `make eval ARGS=--real`).
- **Small sample.** 26 clean and 12 hard test invoices: a single invoice moves a per-type
  number by 20-50 percentage points, and the clean field accuracy by about ±5 points (95%
  interval). The hard subset has only 2 invoices per kind. Small differences between runs or
  file types are not meaningful.
- **The hard subsets are still synthetic damage,** with only 2 invoices per kind per split.
  Noise, blur, shear, fading and light fall-off are generated on clean renders, and the
  phone photos fill the frame, so page-edge detection is not exercised by them. Real phone
  photos also have folds, real shadows, perspective and motion blur, so even the hard
  numbers (75.0% before, 88.9% after) are likely optimistic for the worst real inputs.
- **One author.** The same person (and assistant) designed the system and the dataset, so the
  dataset shares the system's blind spots: it contains what we thought of.
- **LLM variance.** Temperature is 0, but providers don't guarantee identical output, so
  a re-run can differ by an invoice or two.
- **Cost is an upper bound.** Most input tokens are prompt-cache hits, which providers
  usually bill at a discount, but they are priced here at the full input rate.
- **Timing is local.** Measured in Docker on a development laptop with the default worker
  and LLM concurrency, and provider latency varies by time of day.

## How to run

```bash
make eval                      # dataset -> isolated stack -> score -> docs + dashboard
make eval ARGS=--skip-assistant  # skip the 15-question assistant eval
make eval ARGS=--real          # also score your hand-labelled eval/dataset/real/
```

Needs `LLM_PROVIDER` and its key in `.env`; set `LLM_PRICE_INPUT_PER_MTOK` and
`LLM_PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_MTOK` for a cost estimate. Raw results go to `eval/results/`, and the
headline goes to the dashboard (`/dashboard`, "Latest evaluation").
